answer: Work-stamped bonds defeat sybils: every agent must first prove sustained, peer-verified output before its votes carry weight, so flooding cheap identities adds no pigment to the decision. Each account is anchored to a single verifiable origin, and a haven of reputation only forms where many independent agents confirm the same honest history. When colluders try to herd a fake meadow of clones toward one outcome, a slashing rule that confiscates the entire cluster's bonds makes the attack unprofitable, while a real majority's earned weight stays intact.
